pathr: frictionless file paths

Source: R/pathr-package.R
pathr-package.Rd

Working with files in R on Windows means a small but constant friction: backslashes R will not accept, a file explorer you keep switching to and from, and the same chores repeated for every new file. Each function here takes one of those off your plate.

The functions

  • Grab a path without typing it: browse_files(), a keyboard-driven file browser that hands the marked paths back to R – or a call that reads them

  • See a path on disk: open_in_explorer() from the console, and addin_open_in_explorer() from wherever the cursor is

  • Turn pasted Windows paths into valid R: addin_paste_path(), addin_fix_path(), addin_flip_backslash(), and addin_text_to_vector() for a list of them

The addin_*() functions are RStudio addins: call them from the Addins menu or the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), or bind them to a keyboard shortcut under Tools -> Modify Keyboard Shortcuts. vignette("pathr") walks through all of it.

Why a package of its own

The addins were born in daos, a general toolbox. They moved out because they are used in every RStudio session regardless of project, so they should install without the data-wrangling stack daos brings along.
